headline: AI share crash puts world financial stability at risk, warns IMF
summary: The IMF's Global Financial Stability Report warns that the AI sector's high valuations and increasing debt could trigger a global market correction. Concentrated exposures and circular financing arrangements heighten the risk.
details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has warned that a potential AI share price crash, rippling across global markets, is putting world financial stability at risk. In its twice-yearly Global Financial Stability Report, the IMF highlighted sky-high valuations for AI companies and their increasing debt pile as reasons for elevated risks.

The IMF cautioned that the consequences of an AI correction could be global, with Asian markets most exposed after the US. While the UK and euro area might be more insulated, investors with US holdings would still face significant impact.

Athanasios Vamvakidis, deputy director of the IMF’s monetary and capital department, noted that the rest of the world's exposure to US assets, particularly AI, is at an all-time high. This currently supports the global economy through wealth effects, but a market correction could have broad implications.

An AI crash was identified as one of three "salient risks" to stability by the IMF, alongside rising government borrowing costs and the threat of a major cyber-attack. This trio of factors could act as "plausible near-term catalysts for a sharp tightening of financial conditions and market turmoil."

The IMF's analysis underscored the interconnected nature of large AI companies and the high levels of borrowing funding investment in the sector. Weaker or less durable investment and profitability in AI could trigger a correction, exacerbated by rising leverage, concentrated exposures, and circular financing arrangements.

The "magnificent seven" big tech stocks now account for over 35% of the S&P 500 share index in the US, a significant rise from 12% a decade ago. Their total market capitalization has increased by more than 50% in the past two years, yet the IMF questions if the successful rollout of AI truly requires such massive investment.

The report also highlighted growing leverage underpinning the current boom, which could amplify the effects of a crash. This includes soaring debts contracted by the companies themselves, hedge fund investment in the sector, and retail investors borrowing to speculate in AI stocks.

These growing sources of leverage heighten the potential for forced selling and surges in equity volatility during an AI-led market downturn. The IMF also pointed to the prevalence of "circular financing" deals, tying stronger AI companies to weaker partners in the same sector, potentially exacerbating the impact of a share price correction.

headline_marked: [[Google Wallet gets receipt scanning]] and more with latest Play Services update
headline: Google Wallet gets receipt scanning and more with latest Play Services update
summary: Users can now scan and add receipts directly to Google Wallet, giving it an advantage over competitors. The update also streamlines Google Pay on Chrome for Android for more seamless transactions.
details: Google Wallet has received several handy new features as part of the Google Play Services v26.40 update. The most significant addition is the ability to scan and add physical receipts directly into the app, enhancing its functionality beyond just cards and passes.

This new receipt scanning capability gives Google Wallet a slight advantage over other mobile wallet solutions. While Google has not yet clarified the full scope of supported receipt types or global availability, it marks a notable expansion of the app's utility.

The update also improves Google Pay on Chrome for Android, allowing users to skip the Payment Request interface when their name, email, and phone number are already provided to merchants. This aims to make online checkout processes much more seamless.

Furthermore, Google has enhanced merchant names in Google Wallet transaction notifications, providing clearer details on where payments were made. An in-app message center has also been introduced, expected to highlight major new features to users.

Beyond Google Wallet, the Play Services update includes security and privacy improvements for Android WebView, now at version 156. The Google Play Store also gets updates, including 'summarized insights and direct citations from real user reviews with Ask Play' to help users with app decisions.
